title: Noninvasive, label-free image approaches to predict multimodal molecular markers in pluripotency assessment.
authors: Akiyoshi, Ryutaro; Hase, Takeshi; Sathiyananthavel, Mayuri; Ghosh, Samik; Kitano, Hiroaki; Yachie, Ayako
one_liner_zh: 该文用机器学习分析干细胞图像预测多能性标记物，不涉及蛋白质-DNA互作或结合建模，与本课题无关。
abstract: Manufacturing regenerative medicine requires continuous monitoring of pluripotent cell culture and quality assessment while eliminating cell destruction and contaminants. In this study, we employed a novel method to monitor the pluripotency of stem cells through image analysis, avoiding the traditionally used invasive procedures. This approach employs machine learning algorithms to analyze stem cell images to predict the expression of pluripotency markers, such as OCT4 and NANOG, without physically interacting with or harming cells. We cultured induced pluripotent stem cells under various conditions to induce different pluripotent states and imaged the cells using bright-field microscopy. Pluripotency states of induced pluripotent stem cells were assessed using invasive methods, including qPCR, immunostaining, flow cytometry, and RNA sequencing. Unsupervised and semi-supervised learning models were applied to evaluate the results and accurately predict the pluripotency of the cells using only image analysis. Our approach directly links images to invasive assessment results, making the analysis of cell labeling and annotation of cells in images by experts dispensable. This core achievement not only contributes for safer and more reliable stem cell research but also opens new avenues for real-time monitoring and quality control in regenerative medicine manufacturing. Our research fills an important gap in the field by providing a viable, noninvasive alternative to traditional invasive methods for assessing pluripotency. This innovation is expected to make a significant contribution to improving regenerative medicine manufacturing because it will enable a more detailed and feasible understanding of cellular status during the manufacturing process.
abstract_zh: 制造再生医学需要对多能细胞培养进行持续监测和质量评估，同时消除细胞破坏和污染物。在本研究中，我们采用了一种新方法，通过图像分析监测干细胞的多能性，避免了传统使用的侵入性程序。该方法利用机器学习算法分析干细胞图像，以预测多能性标志物（如OCT4和NANOG）的表达，而无需物理接触或伤害细胞。我们在不同条件下培养诱导多能干细胞，以诱导不同的多能状态，并使用明场显微镜对细胞进行成像。通过侵入性方法评估诱导多能干细胞的多能状态，包括qPCR、免疫染色、流式细胞术和RNA测序。应用无监督和半监督学习模型来评估结果，并仅通过图像分析准确预测细胞的多能性。我们的方法直接将图像与侵入性评估结果联系起来，使得专家对图像中细胞的标记和注释变得不必要。这一核心成就不仅有助于更安全、更可靠的干细胞研究，还为再生医学制造中的实时监测和质量控制开辟了新途径。我们的研究通过提供一种可行的、非侵入性的替代传统侵入性方法评估多能性的方案，填补了该领域的重要空白。这一创新预计将对改善再生医学制造做出重大贡献，因为它将使制造过程中细胞状态的更详细和可行的理解成为可能。
